key_insight: A composition gradient in as-deposited crystalline GST films produces predictable, broadband optical tuning, and femtosecond laser writing can further reconfigure the local response.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a scalable route to spatially programmable photonic components whose optical properties are set by both growth composition and post-processing.
method: Single CVD growth created a compositional series spanning Ge3Sb2Te6, Ge2Sb2Te5, and GeSb2Te4.
Correlated composition with microstructure, morphology, and optical response across 400–1700 nm.
Used femtosecond laser irradiation for localized optical reconfiguration without relying on amorphous-crystalline cycling.
evidence_signal: The absorption minimum shifted from 815.9 nm to 889.8 nm with a 5.9-fold intensity change across the composition gradient, indicating strong composition-dependent optical variation.
watch_item: The reported tuning is demonstrated in as-deposited crystalline films, so device-level stability and repeatability under long-term thermal or optical cycling still need validation.
paper_title: Laser induced optical reconfiguration in Ge_Sb_Te Films with composition dependent response
